title: Zoomed all the way out: the outdoor skyline (companion card)
question: Same change, outdoor terrain instead of the lab — does more resolution still improve it here, or does the rock lose its texture?
context_md:
Companion to the lab card. Same change: grow the render buffer at the widest zoom-out so more world cells reach a pixel of their own, instead of fifteen in sixteen being discarded.

**This scene is why it is worth asking twice.** On the lab bed the finer buffer plainly wins — plants get their real shape back. On bare rock it is not obvious: the per-cell shade jitter that gives stone its grain is drawn at 4x4 blocks today, and at one cell per pixel that grain becomes fine enough to read as **smooth** rather than as texture.

All three show the identical patch of world at the identical size on screen; the coarse one is magnified back up exactly as your monitor already does it.
